title: termag environment definition
description: What an agent needs to work on a set of repositories: the repositories, the box's resources, how to set it up and run it, the ports it serves and the names of the secrets its steps need. It is a .termag/environment.json in a repository, a file an environment points at (repo : branch : path), or an inline environment's definition. termag reads repos and resources when a box is made, and the box runs setup, run, ports, seed, stop and secrets ("The steps"); slots, env, envFile and host are not used yet. Unknown keys are ignored.

$schema.description: This schema's URL, for editors. Ignored by termag.

repos.description: The repositories a project made from this environment holds, in checkout order. Two or more make a multi-repo project. In a file an environment points at, the file's own repository is included whether it is listed or not.

branch.description: The branch the checkout tracks. Absent, the repository's default branch.

path.description: The checkout's directory: on a box made from the environment, ~/code/<path>; in a multi-repo project, its directory under the project. Absent, the repository's name.

resources.description: The box's size: a preset, or minimums EC2 matches to a Graviton m/r type. An explicit --size or picker choice wins over it.

oneOf.description: small is 2 vCPU / 8 GiB, medium 4 / 16, large 8 / 32.

vcpu.description: At least this many vCPUs (at most 8).

memoryGiB.description: At least this much memory, in GiB (at most 32).

diskGiB.description: The root disk, in GiB (50 to 300), of a new box made from it.

base.description: full: termag's whole box. empty: termag's core only, and setup does the rest. The owner confirms it at creation; an explicit choice wins.

setup.description: An idempotent, incremental bootstrap after checkout: system packages, dependencies, codegen. It gets no secrets, even ones secrets names, and no owner identity: an environment pool runs it before the box has an owner. termag runs it again whenever a repository's HEAD has moved since it last succeeded, so a rerun should do only what changed. A string runs in the file's repository; a map runs each repository's command in its checkout, in the order written.

run.description: Brings the app up. A string runs in the file's repository; a map starts every entry at once, each in its own tmux window.

seed.description: Optional, after run: demo data and fixtures. A string or a repository → command map, run in order.

stop.description: Optional: what termag-env down runs before it closes the session, for a run that daemonizes. A string or a repository → command map, run in order; a failing stop is logged and the session closes anyway.

ports.description: What run serves, and how to tell it is up. The first is what a preview opens.

name.description: What the port is, e.g. frontend.

port.description: The port, or per slot: base + step × (slot − 1).

health.description: A path that answers once the port is up, e.g. /api/health.

path.description: The page the port's link and a preview open, e.g. /termag/. Absent, /.

secrets.description: Names of the environment variables run and seed need, resolved by termag's credential delivery. Names only, never values. setup never gets them.

slots.description: One instance per workstream on a box, slot 1..max; slot 1 is the owner's. Without slots, one instance per box.

env.description: Variables for every step. ${slot} and resolved secrets are expanded.

envFile.description: A gitignored file, relative to the file's repository, that termag also writes env and resolved secrets into, in a managed block.

host.description: The loopback address the ports are on; ${slot} is expanded. Default 127.0.0.1.
